<reason>CON won the live mechanism fight the motion actually requires. After conceding that governments may write industry-specific floors, CON showed PRO’s distinctive device—a private table with extension—is either a statute wearing a bargaining label once seats, vetoes, and a bare product are stacked on, or the insider-cartel harm of extension. PRO kept a real coverage/fissuring case but never showed why bargaining, not public statute plus enforcement, is necessary on net; the rural-worker matching reply stayed thin, and a clipped first rebuttal cost recovery.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON’s statute-versus-table dilemma in R2 (A4.1–A4.2), which turned PRO’s own guardrails into proof that constrained bargaining adds nothing and unconstrained bargaining adds the harm.</best_rebuttal>
